claims.text: Mild post-deposition annealing promotes short-range chemical ordering in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs.
Mild post-deposition annealing relaxes intrinsic strain in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs.
Increased chemical ordering and strain relaxation reduce pinning of the magnetostructural phase boundary.
Reduced phase-boundary pinning lowers the energy barrier for the field-induced magnetostructural transition.
Lowering the transition barrier broadens the magnetocaloric temperature span.
Lowering the transition barrier reduces hysteresis during low-applied-field cooling cycles.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys possess a largely single-phase hexagonal state.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys contain quenched-in internal stresses.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys have high defect and disorder levels.
A suitable mild anneal can permit partial ordering and strain relaxation without significant phase segregation or grain growth.
Annealing-induced ordering and stress reduction lower the nucleation barrier for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
A lower nucleation barrier makes the first-order phase change less abrupt.
The annealed material can retain a strong magnetocaloric response despite reduced hysteresis.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, annealed samples will exhibit a slightly broadened but still large magnetic entropy change.
Annealed samples will exhibit less thermal hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline during low-field cycling.
Annealed samples will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline during low-field cycling.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs undergo a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with a large, hysteretic entropy change.
High internal strain and disorder cause the baseline hysteresis.
The predicted annealing effect should extend to similarly composed and structured thin films or rapidly quenched ribbons.
The predicted effect may fail when initial disorder is extremely high or annealing produces secondary phases.
